headline: Not yet: yields at 5.15% and Nvidia's slide hold pressure at 71
summary: Nvidia fell 2.0% on Friday 13 November, a sixth weekly loss, and closed below $4T. The 10-year yield rose to 5.15% as a December Fed hike gained backing. The Nasdaq fell 0.9%, yet both indexes won the week. [24][2][13]

signals.label: 10-year Treasury yield
signals.eli5: The interest rate the US government pays to borrow for ten years. When it rises, safe bonds compete with shares, and expensive stocks are the first to look less attractive.

signals.label: Hyperscaler capex ÷ cash flow
signals.note: Q3: the four now spend more than they earn; score 100
signals.eli5: What Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon and Meta spend on data centres and chips, as a share of the cash their businesses make. Near 100% means they spend about all they earn.

signals.label: Margin debt growth, y/y
signals.eli5: How much more money investors have borrowed from their brokers to buy shares than a year ago. Borrowed bets pile up in a boom and get sold in a hurry when prices fall.

signals.label: Nvidia weekly move
signals.note: sixth straight weekly loss; below $4T market cap
signals.eli5: Nvidia makes the chips the AI boom runs on, so its share price is the market's running bet on AI. A fall in it says confidence in that bet is slipping.

analysis: The basket scores 69.6: fragility 80.4, trigger 37.1, confirmation 88.1. Price to sales (3.73), household equities (48.2% of financial assets), subprime auto delinquency (6.23%) and hyperscaler capex at 115% of operating cash flow sit beyond any prior burst; CAPE is 39.95. The BIS credit gap, at −11.3 points, and a Fed that has cut over 12 months are the calmest readings. [4][9][15][17][3][11][12]

On Friday 13 November the Nasdaq fell 0.91% to 25,136.27 and the S&P 500 0.4% to 7,561.67, though both finished the week higher. Nvidia sank 2.01% and closed below a $4 trillion market value for the first time since July 2025, down 12.75% on the week, after CEO Jensen Huang's resignation; analysts fear his successor may back the AI ecosystem less. [1][2][24]

The 10-year Treasury yield rose to 5.15% on 13 November in the Treasury data as hot inflation prints firmed bets on a December Fed hike. Against that, FactSet puts the forward P/E at 17.7, below its 19.1 ten-year average, with Q3 earnings up 31.4%. Anthropic is marketing its IPO near $1.3trn. [23] Why 71: the basket sits at 69.6 and the rate path and Nvidia slide add about one. [13][2][22]

indicators.label: S&P 500 Shiller CAPE ratio
indicators.eli5: Share prices divided by ten years of average company profits, so one good or bad year cannot fool it. The higher it is, the more people are paying for each dollar of profit.

indicators.label: S&P 500 price to sales
indicators.detail: Price to trailing 12-month sales, 12 Nov 2026, multpl.com
indicators.eli5: The value of the 500 biggest US companies divided by their sales. Sales are harder to dress up than profits, so a high ratio says prices have run far ahead of what firms sell.

indicators.label: Nasdaq Composite ÷ S&P 500
indicators.eli5: How the tech-heavy Nasdaq compares with the broader S&P 500. When this climbs, money is piling into tech faster than into everything else, which is what past bubbles looked like.

indicators.label: Margin debt growth, year on year
indicators.detail: FINRA margin debit balances, Sep 2026 vs Sep 2025
indicators.eli5: How much more money investors have borrowed from their brokers to buy shares than a year ago. Borrowed bets pile up in a boom and get sold in a hurry when prices fall.

indicators.label: Household equities, share of financial assets
indicators.detail: Fed Z.1 households, Q2 2026, FRED BOGZ1FL153064486Q
indicators.eli5: The slice of ordinary households' savings that sits in shares. The bigger the slice, the fewer new buyers are left to push prices up, and the harder a fall would hit.

indicators.label: Semiconductor index ÷ S&P 500
indicators.eli5: The main chip-maker index compared with the S&P 500. Chips are the picks and shovels of the AI boom, so this shows how much of the market's bet is riding on it.

indicators.label: Hyperscaler capex ÷ cash flow
indicators.eli5: What Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon and Meta spend on data centres and chips, as a share of the cash their businesses make. Near 100% means they spend about all they earn.

indicators.label: TSMC monthly revenue growth
indicators.detail: October 2026 revenue NT$586.89bn, TSMC investor site
indicators.eli5: How fast sales are growing at TSMC, the company that makes nearly every advanced AI chip. Its order book is an early read on whether AI demand is still speeding up.

indicators.label: US high-yield spread (ICE BofA OAS)
indicators.detail: ICE BofA US high-yield option-adjusted spread, FRED
indicators.eli5: The extra interest risky companies pay to borrow compared with the US government. A small gap means lenders are relaxed; a widening gap often comes just before trouble.

indicators.label: BIS US credit-to-GDP gap
indicators.detail: Credit-to-GDP gap, Q1 2026, BIS statistics API
indicators.eli5: How far total US borrowing has run ahead of its usual path relative to the size of the economy. Near zero is routine; a big positive gap has come before most credit busts.

indicators.label: Fed funds target, 12-month change
indicators.detail: Upper bound 4.00% vs 4.25% a year earlier (−25bp), FRED
indicators.eli5: How much the Fed has raised its main interest rate over the past year. Higher rates make borrowing dearer and have pricked past bubbles; a year of cuts counts as zero here.

indicators.label: 10-year Treasury yield
indicators.eli5: The interest rate the US government pays to borrow for ten years. When it rises, safe bonds compete with shares, and expensive stocks are the first to look less attractive.

indicators.label: US unemployment rate (U-3)
indicators.eli5: The share of people looking for work who cannot find it. Very low unemployment is where booms peak; once it starts rising, the economy is usually already turning.

indicators.label: Subprime auto loan delinquency
indicators.detail: Fitch subprime auto 60+ day index, Sep 2026
indicators.eli5: The share of riskier car loans more than two months behind on payments. Car loans go bad early when households are squeezed, so this is an early warning for the economy.

indicators.label: Chicago Fed financial conditions (NFCI)
indicators.detail: NFCI weekly, week to 6 Nov 2026, Chicago Fed via FRED
indicators.eli5: The Chicago Fed's one-number summary of how easy money is: credit, borrowing and market stress. Below zero means easier than usual, the conditions bubbles grow in.

composite.reason: Nvidia fell a sixth straight week and hike bets firmed, partly offset by a winning week for the indexes and a 17.7 forward P/E; the anchor sits at 69.6.

fundamentals.label: S&P 500 forward 12-month P/E
fundamentals.eli5: Share prices divided by the profits analysts expect over the next year. Below its ten-year average, prices are not running ahead of expected earnings.

fundamentals.label: S&P 500 Q3 earnings growth
fundamentals.note: blended, 88% reported; third straight quarter above 25%
fundamentals.eli5: How much more profit the 500 biggest US companies made this quarter than a year ago. Fast growth means real earnings, not just hope, back prices.

fundamentals.label: TSMC October revenue growth
fundamentals.note: NT$586.89bn; 2026 revenue to date up 43.3% on 2025
fundamentals.eli5: How fast sales are growing at TSMC, the company that makes nearly every advanced AI chip. Its order book is an early read on whether AI demand is still speeding up.
